data.finalText:
The protected `internal/action` executor already does the audit and idempotency work, so the candidate only needs to call it and convert its types to the protocol types.
`POST /purchases/bulk-approve` now writes the approval audit and stores an idempotent result in the same transaction. It builds and passes `go vet` and `go test ./...`, but there are no test files, so nothing has been run against a real database yet.

I only changed `internal/candidate/approval.go`. Instead of writing its own SQL, it now creates the protected Action executor once with `action.New(ctx, pool, "")`, with no fault injection. Each request goes to `Executor.BulkApprove`, and its results come back as `protocol.Result`. Its rejections become `protocol.Rejection`, so the HTTP layer sets the status. Other errors pass through unchanged: a duplicate-row error still returns 409, and anything else returns 503.

From reading the protected executor, it already does everything else the spec asks for:
- Purchase updates, ApprovalAudit rows and the completed ActionRequest record are all written in one transaction, so a failed batch changes nothing.
- A transaction lock on operation+tenant+actor+key makes concurrent requests with the same key run one at a time. A repeat with the same ID set returns the saved response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A repeat with a different set gets 409.
- Targets are locked for update and re-checked, so when two batches with different keys overlap, only one succeeds and the loser's other targets are left unchanged.
- `requestHash` follows the required SHA-256 format, and the stored response holds the sorted `approvedIds`.
- Identity comes only from the authenticated bearer token, not from client headers.
- All other paths still go to the original server, so the old APIs are unchanged.

I didn't run `python3 visible_smoke.py` because no separate public test service was supplied. Rollback, replay and the concurrent cases still need to be checked against a live database.
